text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Parties in Bulgaria's parliament accepted a proposal by the ruling Union of Democratic Forces that parliament holds extraordinary sessions this month to speed up approval of the 1997 budget law prior to the introduction of a currency board system on July 1. @

-- The World Bank agreed with Bulgaria's proposal to introduce a temporary tax on grain exports, to be in effect by end-autumn, to avoid possible grain shortages, parliament's economy committee chairman Nikola Nikolov said.

-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry said its high-ranking officials should not be members of companies' ruling bodies, following appointemnt of a ministry's chief secretary on the board of directors of the Neftochim oil refinery. @

-- The Bulgarian Telecommunications Company had stabilised its financies ahead of a planned partial privatisation and was aiming for a bid that would value it at $4 to $6 billion, company director Marian Dragostinov said. The stake to be offered for sale is yet to be decided by the government.

-- Kuwait will extend an initial $40 million credit to Bulgaria from the Kuwaiti Development Fund for reconstruction of Sofia airport, Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov said, wrapping up a three-day visit to the arab state.

-- Police searched the offices of ailing Slavyani Bank for possible evidence of extended uncollateralised credits of over two billion levs by its former directors. The private bank has been in receivership since September 1996, and an insolvency case has been launched against it by the central bank.
-- Prices of imported cigarettes are expected to fall by 15 percent due to the stable lev under a proposal by the trade ministry to be discussed at a cabinet meeting today.
-- Prices of basic foods rose by some five percent last week, price tags in Sofia shops showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
